business_problem: C.H. Robinson needed to automate email-heavy shipment workflows because too many customers still submit routine requests through inconsistent emails and PDFs that force employees to spend hours triaging and manually keying orders.
solution_summary: C.H. Robinson built proprietary AI agents to automate shipment transactions from quoting through pickup, delivery, and in-transit updates. The team started on LangChain for interoperability so they could combine messy customer instructions with order context while retaining the freedom to swap models. As classification between less-than-truckload and full truckload grew more complex, they moved into LangGraph, which made order state easier to understand, track, and update across multi-step workflows. LangGraph Studio then helped prototype and debug those agent interactions visually. The resulting system reads shipping-request emails, connects facts across the email body and attached PDFs, fills in missing information, and creates orders automatically. LangSmith traces the full order-entry process so subject-matter experts and developers can quantify errors, inspect prompts, and catch problems before rollout.

data_flow: Customer emails and attached PDFs enter the proprietary AI workflow, LangChain combines the raw request with order context, LangGraph classifies shipment types and maintains order state while missing details are retrieved, and LangSmith records the end-to-end order-entry trace for review before deployment.
business_outcome: C.H. Robinson automated thousands of daily orders, reduced manual backlog from shipment emails, and freed employees to focus on higher-value customer work while improving speed across the shipping lifecycle.
